newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Russian PM discuss government's work.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Russian PM discuss government's work.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday to discuss the government's work in the first half of this year and tactics for the next six months, Interfax news agency said.

The presidential and government press services declined to comment on the meeting. But Interfax quoted Chernomyrdin as telling Yeltsin at the start of talks in the Kremlin: "On the whole, we have finished the half-year with positive results."

Yeltsin also met Chernomyrdin and his top ministers on Tuesday and told them military reform, payment of wage arrears, protection of domestic industries and health care should be the top priorities for the rest of the year.
Yeltsin drew attention on Wednesday to the need to improve tax collection.
"Tax collection now is the main thing," Interfax quoted the 66-year-old president as saying.
Tax revenues have been lower than budgeted in the first few months of the year, driving the new reformist cabinet into tough measures to try to make companies pay up.
Interfax said Chernomyrdin had praised the work of Russian customs officers for bringing about eight trillion roubles ($1.4 billion) into the state budget in late May and June.
Yeltsin reshuffled the government in March, putting reformers in important positions to reinvigorate market reforms under the veteran Chernomyrdin. He had called the previous cabinet "stagnant".
The government leaders told Yeltsin on Tuesday they had met his demands to pay off a huge backlog of pensions, clearing one of the first major hurdles since the reshuffle.

Yeltsin and his government have been upset by the failure of the communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament to adopt a reform package which the cabinet believes is crucial for moving further economic reforms.
Interfax news agency quoted the Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov as saying he was due to meet Yeltsin on Friday to discuss the legislation.
